title: SC raises compensation for crime victims, citing inflation, severity of offenses
summary: The Supreme Court (SC) has increased the monetary awards for crime victims, taking into account the gravity of offenses, the suffering endured by victims and survivors, and economic realities such as…

blocks.text: The Supreme Court (SC) has increased the monetary awards for crime victims, taking into account the gravity of offenses, the suffering endured by victims and survivors, and economic realities such as inflation.

In a press release on Monday, the SC En Banc announced that it had approved updated guidelines governing the award of civil indemnity ex delicto, moral damages, exemplary damages and temperate damages.

“The value of judicial awards should not remain fixed when the financial and social circumstances underlying them have materially changed. Inflation, cost of living, wage growth, and fiscal stability are relevant considerations in determining appropriate awards,” the SC said.

However, the Court stressed that the review should not be reduced to a mere computation of inflation, noting that damages in criminal cases involving violations of bodily integrity, dignity and personal autonomy cannot be measured solely in monetary terms.
Under the new guidelines, the Court increased the civil indemnity, moral damages and exemplary damages awarded to a child victim who was six years old when the crimes were committed.
The awards were raised as follows:

items: Qualified rape of a minor: P325,000 each, from P100,000
Acts of lasciviousness: P175,000 each, from P50,000

blocks.text: The awards will also earn 6% annual legal interest from the finality of the decision until full payment, the SC said.

Trial courts are also required to direct the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) to refer child victims, with the consent of their guardians, to a Rape Crisis Center for care and support.
The High Court said judges retain the discretion to increase the compensation further, depending on the circumstances of each case.

For crimes resulting in death, the SC set the highest compensation ranges, recognizing that the loss of life is permanent and irreversible. It also established higher baseline awards for intentional killings than for deaths caused by negligence.
The Court ruled that all awards for civil indemnity, moral damages, exemplary damages and temperate damages in criminal cases must follow the updated amounts under the new guidelines.

The amounts will be determined based on the “penalty prescribed by law, the nature and stage of consummation of the offense, the extent of injury or loss, and the lived experience of the victim and survivors.”

“Civil damages are not merely incidental relief in criminal proceedings. They are essential expressions of the law’s recognition of the harm suffered by victims and society’s condemnation of criminal conduct,” the SC said.
Through the updated guidelines, the Court seeks to ensure that monetary awards remain consistent, proportionate to the gravity of offenses and responsive to victims' circumstances, it added.
The ruling was penned by Associate Justice Maria Filomena Singh.— MCG, GMA News
